title: Pluggable RBAC V2 Evaluation Fabric with Explainable Traces & Admin Policy Simulator
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Summary: Implement a pluggable RBAC v2 evaluation fabric that provides a single evaluation API used by API gateway, runtime inference path, and console admin flows. Key differentiators: (1) explainable evaluation traces for audit and debug, (2) a policy simulator embedded in the admin console for safe canarying of rule changes, and (3) a lightweight plugin interface to add new attribute sources (SSO/SAML assertions, admin overrides, request context).

Scope:
- Core: evaluation fabric (gRPC/HTTP interface) with deterministic inputs and versioned policy bundles.
- Middleware: small interceptors for API gateway, runtime inbound, and console backend that translate local context to fabric inputs and enforce decisions with a uniform deny/fallback behavior.
- Observability: structured explainable traces (JSON) emitted to audit pipeline and linked to request traces; metrics for decision latency, cache hit/miss, and rule-match distribution.
- Admin: a policy simulator UI and an API endpoint to dry-run a policy bundle against sampled real requests or synthetic inputs.
- Security: signed policy bundles, ephemeral evaluation keys for runtime consumers, and audit entries for simulator runs.

Design notes and trade-offs:
- Evaluator design: use a deterministic policy execution graph (PEG) that precompiles high-frequency paths. This reduces per-decision CPU but requires a bundle compile step when rules change. We accept a small compile latency (seconds) in exchange for sub-millisecond hot-path evaluation.
- Caching: introduce a two-layer cache: attribute-level short-term cache (100ms TTL) for identity/assertion lookups, and decision-level cache keyed by (subject, resource, action, encoded-context). The decision cache must respect admin overrides and break glass flags.
- Explainability: traces will include which rule fired, intermediate attribute values, and a compact proof-of-evaluation. For privacy, sensitive attributes (PII) are redacted before being sent to the audit pipeline; redaction is governed by a configurable sensitive-attrs list.
- Simulator: runs in read-only mode by default and records audit events when a simulator test is run. The simulator supports 'sampled real request replay' but requires opt-in per-tenant to avoid leaking production payloads.

Acceptance criteria:
- Single evaluation API implemented and documented.
- API, runtime, and console middleware integrated and returning consistent allow/deny decisions for 100% of unit tests.
- Explainable trace JSON emitted for every decision in non-prod and for 1% of production decisions; traces contain rule id, rule source, matched expressions, and redacted attributes.
- Decision P50 < 4ms, P99 < 20ms on standard Dedicated instance with caching enabled.
- Policy simulator accessible in admin console and can run against sampled traffic; simulator runs produce audit log entries.
- Signed policy bundles and a bundle-rotation process implemented; document operational runbook.

Out-of-scope for this ticket: full RBAC policy language extension (to be handled in a follow-up), long-term retention of raw traces beyond the audit-retention window, and per-tenant custom policy language compilers.

risks_and_mitigations:
Risk: decision cache invalidation could lead to incorrect allow when admin overrides occur. Mitigation: implement conservative TTL and explicit invalidation webhook tied to bundle rotation; log invalidation events. Risk: simulator leak of production payloads. Mitigation: require tenant opt-in and redact sensitive fields in replay mode.

Operational runbook stub: https://docs.redwood.ai/confluence/rbac-v2-runbook
testing_plan: Unit tests for rule interpreter and PEG compiled paths; integration tests for middleware adapters across API gateway, runtime request path, and console; load tests for P99 under synthetic traffic patterns; end-to-end simulation tests validating audit entries for simulator runs.
notes_for_oncall: When toggling simulator sampling feature-flags, monitor audit event rate and disk/video retention. If evaluation service latency >50ms for >1min, fail closed for API gateway and notify security channel #sec-rbac with incident template.
